name: Deere & Company

profile.description: Deere & Company designs, manufactures, and distributes agricultural, construction, forestry, and turf care equipment worldwide through four segments: Production and Precision Agriculture, Small Agriculture and Turf, Construction and Forestry, and Financial Services. Technologies include the John Deere Operations Center, See & Spray precision-agriculture computer vision, and a growing fleet of autonomous tractors. Founded in 1837 and headquartered in Moline, Illinois, Deere reported FY2025 revenue of $44.7B (down 12% amid an agricultural equipment downcycle) while its Construction and Forestry order book strengthens on data-center and infrastructure-driven demand.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Under CEO John May, Deere has executed multiple successful launches that redefined its category — the fully autonomous 8R tractor and See & Spray computer-vision weed-detection system are commercialized products, not concepts, and the company's market cap has more than doubled to over $180B during his tenure [5]. AI Deployment (2/2): See & Spray and autonomous tractors are AI products actively shipping to and generating revenue from customers, not internal pilots, built on a decade-plus 'Smart Industrial' strategy [5]. Market Share (2/2): Deere remains the #1 global producer of production agriculture equipment, and its Construction & Forestry segment is gaining share as AI data-center construction fuels a sales boom, with FY2026 segment sales guided up ~20% [2][3]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Construction order backlog is over 80% filled for FY2026 with visibility extending into FY2027, though specific next-generation product timelines beyond incremental autonomy rollout are less detailed than a defense-style pipeline [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Deere's ~$1.9-2.1B annual R&D spend (roughly 4-5% of revenue) is solid for heavy machinery but not clearly top-quartile versus peers on a comparable basis.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Deere's purpose of enabling those 'linked to the land' to feed, fuel, and shelter the world is specific and connects to a larger cause, reinforced by nearly 190 years of continuous operation, though it is undercut by a real credibility gap discussed below. Community Impact (1/2): The John Deere Foundation funds agricultural education and rural community programs, but no distinctive dollar-specific initiatives comparable to sector leaders were found in current research. Employee Retention (1/2): The company's century-plus Midwest manufacturing culture suggests reasonable stability, but no specific tenure or turnover data is available, and Deere has trimmed headcount at several plants during the 2024-2026 ag downcycle. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying in the past 12 months. Critically, a multi-state FTC/Attorneys General right-to-repair lawsuit — settled in mid-2026, requiring Deere to open access to diagnostic codes and repair manuals for farmers and independent shops — directly contradicts the company's stated farmer-partnership ethos and tempers the mission-floor score [4].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored using the Growth-sleeve formula (PEG, ROE, and 5yr Revenue CAGR at 2x weight). ROE of 18.24% clears the 15% target (score 1.0, 2x weight) and Forward PEG of 1.58 sits reasonably between the 1.0 target and 3.0 floor (score 0.71, 2x weight), reflecting still-solid profitability despite the cycle trough [6]. FY2025 revenue fell 12% to $44.7B, the bottom of the ag downcycle, dragging the 3-year revenue CAGR to roughly -4.5% (score 0.03, 2x weight) even as trailing-twelve-month growth has re-accelerated to +4.9% amid the Construction & Forestry rebound (score 0.83) [1][2]. D/E of 230% is elevated versus the 70% target, largely reflecting the captive Financial Services leasing book (score 0.30), Forward P/E of 29.5 is moderate (score 0.76), and profit margin of 10.2% is roughly half the 20% target (score 0.51). Daily dollar volume of roughly $820M provides ample liquidity, comfortably clearing the $1M floor [6].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: Deere's core business is physical heavy-equipment manufacturing and dealer-network distribution — AI structurally cannot replace tractors, combines, or excavators, and the company's own precision-ag AI (See & Spray, autonomous tractors, John Deere Operations Center) makes it a beneficiary rather than a target of AI substitution [5]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Deere generates quantifiable, growing revenue from AI-enabled precision-ag subscriptions and is a direct beneficiary of the AI data-center buildout, which is driving a reported 'sales boom' and roughly 20% guided growth in its Construction & Forestry segment as hyperscalers order site-prep and earthmoving equipment [3].

infinite_game.summary: Deere has a genuinely resilient, multi-generational purpose around enabling those who feed and build the world, and has shown real courage investing in autonomy through a painful ag downcycle — but a recently settled right-to-repair lawsuit exposes a real gap between stated farmer-partnership values and revenue-protecting service practices, and earnings commentary still leans on share-and-margin language typical of a finite competitor.

just_cause.analysis: The purpose of enabling those linked to the land is genuine and has persisted across nearly two centuries and multiple leadership transitions, but the FTC/state right-to-repair settlement shows the cause has been only partially lived rather than fully validated by practice [4].

trusting_teams.analysis: Deere's Midwest manufacturing culture is stable and long-tenured, but plant-level layoffs during the 2024-2026 ag downcycle and no specific published retention data keep this at an adequate rather than exceptional level.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Earnings commentary and investor materials emphasize market-share leadership and margin dominance over CNH and AGCO rather than framing competitors as sources of mutual improvement.

existential_flexibility.analysis: The 'Smart Industrial' shift toward autonomy and software-attached equipment is a meaningful evolution of the core business, but Deere remains fundamentally an equipment manufacturer rather than having undergone a full business-model reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Deere sustained R&D and capex investment in autonomy and precision ag through the worst of the current ag downcycle rather than slashing innovation spend to protect near-term margins, a real if not dramatic act of long-term-over-short-term prioritization.

investment_thesis: Deere is the dominant global player in production agriculture and a fast-growing beneficiary of AI-driven infrastructure spend through its Construction & Forestry segment, where order backlogs are over 80% filled for FY2026 with visibility into FY2027 and segment sales are guided up roughly 20% [2][3]. The ag equipment business appears to be bottoming in 2026 per management's own commentary, and Deere's precision-ag technology stack (See & Spray, autonomous tractors, Operations Center) gives it a durable, AI-enabled moat that peers have struggled to replicate [5].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on cyclicality and trust: FY2025 revenue fell 12% to $44.7B and the trailing 3-year revenue CAGR is negative, EPS has fallen from $34.63 (FY2023) to $18.50 (FY2025), and Forward P/E of 29.5x already prices in a meaningful recovery that depends on farm income improving from currently depressed levels [1][6]. The settled FTC/state right-to-repair litigation is a reputational and regulatory overhang that could pressure high-margin parts and service revenue going forward as farmers gain more independent repair access [4].
key_catalysts: Construction & Forestry order book over 80% filled for FY2026 with backlog visibility into FY2027, driven by AI data-center and infrastructure construction demand [2][3]
Management's own guidance that 2026 marks the bottom of the multi-year agricultural equipment downcycle, with consensus FY2027 EPS growth of nearly 28%
Continued precision-ag subscription attach (John Deere Operations Center, See & Spray) expanding higher-margin recurring software and data revenue
key_risks: Persistently weak farm income and high global grain/oilseed inventories could extend the ag equipment downcycle beyond management's 2026 bottom-call
Right-to-repair settlement terms requiring open diagnostic and repair access could compress high-margin aftermarket parts and service revenue over time [4]
Elevated D/E (230%) tied to the captive Financial Services leasing book increases sensitivity to credit-quality deterioration among ag and construction dealers

backlog.note: Deere does not disclose a formal dollar backlog like a defense contractor. Construction & Forestry order books have risen over 60% since November and are more than 80% filled for FY2026 production with visibility into FY2027 [2][3], while the Production & Precision Agriculture order book remains at the trough of a multi-year downcycle management expects to bottom in 2026 [1][2] — a genuinely mixed, segment-divergent picture.
